evidence: The new guard says 'The only valid reason to edit this file is to correct an inaccuracy in the tmux protocol' while SPEC.md still carries '(library)'-labeled sections the reviewer named; commit 24574d3 appends a sentence acknowledging those legacy notes and pointing at tmux-audit-q17, which removes the contradiction.
guidance_note: Before writing an absolute scope rule at the top of a document, grep the same document for content the rule forbids and either acknowledge or remove it in the same commit.

evidence: The wait-exit row read 'see also `detach()` in §26.2' and §26 was deleted by this PR; 24574d3 replaces the cross-reference with a direct protocol description.
guidance_note: When deleting a numbered section, grep the file for references to that section number (here '§26') before committing.

evidence: 'builds ergonomic API on top of it' is missing an article; the agent changed it to 'builds an ergonomic API'. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the sentence is present unchanged in the round-0 hunk at e89c8ff, and 24574d3 did not touch it.

F2's fix in 24574d3 rewrote the wait-exit row to say 'an empty line on stdin is what unblocks it', an exclusive claim that contradicts §8.1's 'an empty line or EOF'; the agent then aligned the row with §8.1.
guidance_note: When rewriting a row to drop a dangling reference, take the replacement wording from the spec's canonical section for that behavior (§8.1 here) instead of paraphrasing from the old row.

narrative: A docs-only PR removing §26 and adding a protocol-only guard. Round 0 found a guard that contradicted the file's own legacy library sections, and a dangling §26.2 reference. A rerun on the fix commit found a grammar nit that was already in the original, plus a wait-exit row whose rewritten wording now contradicted §8.1. Round 3 would have happened for the grammar nit anyway, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: The F2 fix paraphrased a behavior description instead of copying the spec's own canonical wording, which created a second finding in the same row.

evidence: The reviewer's only evidence is that sibling workflows pin @v4. In #75/F2 of this same batch the agent showed `gh api repos/actions/checkout/releases` listing v6.0.0–v6.0.3, and code-review.yml's own Review job going green on @v6. The agent accepted 'v6 does not exist' without checking, and hand-edited a file that the install script regenerates; #74's 8261f3d puts v6 straight back.
guidance_note: When a reviewer claims an action or package version does not exist, check the release list (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases`) and the workflow's own run status before changing anything, and never hand-edit an installer-generated workflow.

narrative: A cleanup PR deleting TmuxClientLike, dead bridge methods and IMPL.md. Its one finding was a false claim from the reviewer's knowledge cutoff that actions/checkout@v6 does not exist. The agent accepted it and downgraded a generated workflow to v4. The installer rewrote it to v6 in the next PR, which cost another false finding there.
guidance_observations: The agent treated a reviewer's factual claim about an external registry as settled when one `gh api` call would have refuted it; two PRs later the agent did make that check and pushed back correctly.

evidence: The test is the named 'shared-decoder' lesson, whose acceptance criterion the agent quotes as 'the decoder is called once per chunk regardless of consumer count'. Output assertions cannot tell one shared decoder from two separate ones, so removing the spy would make the lesson untestable. The coupling to TextDecoder.prototype is real but small.

Commit 8261f3d is the install script putting back the @v6 it generates (the agent's reply says 'the install script wrote' it). It is not a fix for any finding in this PR, so the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag has no in-PR cause. The premise is false: #75/F2 shows v6.0.0–v6.0.3 releases and a green run on @v6. The agent reverted the generator's output to v4 a second time.
guidance_note: When the generator rewrites a line you previously hand-changed, treat it as a sign the hand change was wrong: verify the reviewer's claim, and if the template really is wrong, change the generator instead of reverting its output.

narrative: A named hard-won-lessons test suite. In round 0 the agent correctly pushed back on removing a decode-count spy that is the lesson's actual contract. Round 1 flagged actions/checkout@v6 after the installer re-wrote the workflow that #73 had hand-downgraded. The agent again accepted the false 'v6 does not exist' claim and reverted the generated line.
guidance_observations: The same false finding recurred across PRs because the agent kept fighting the generator's output instead of checking the claim once.

evidence: The hunk shows `try { this.ws.send(encodePaneOutput(msg)); } catch {}`, which widens the TOCTOU catch so it also swallows serializer errors. The fix hoists `const frame = encodePaneOutput(msg)` above the try, matching the old code's scope.
guidance_note: When converting a closure to a class method, keep the exact extent of any existing try/catch; do not inline a computed value into the guarded expression.

evidence: The agent showed `gh api repos/actions/checkout/releases` listing v6.0.0–v6.0.3, and code-review.yml's own Review job passing on @v6. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: bf2ee1c only reformats source files and does not touch the workflow, and the v6 line was already flagged in the round-2 summary. Citing no-silent-failure for a version downgrade was a pasted token.

narrative: A refactor of BytesSink destinations into classes. Round 0 correctly caught that a try/catch had widened over the pure encode, and the hoist fix was clean. Round 3 raised the false actions/checkout@v6 claim again. This time the agent refuted it with the release list and a green run, which is the check that #73 and #74 skipped.
guidance_observations: The pushback here was correct, but it attached an irrelevant law token; the factual evidence carried the argument alone.

evidence: The agent concedes the drop and argues it is harmless: pre-ready, nothing can be paused because Pause requires a delivered command. That holds if the suppressor is the only source of pauses. The packet does not show whether tmux's own pause-after could pause a pane before onTransportReady recomputes, so the argument cannot be confirmed. no-mode-explosion does not describe redundant Continue traffic.
guidance_note: When an action is dropped because its transport is not ready, write down in the original PR why the dropped action is safe, or replay it; don't leave the reviewer to discover the gap.

narrative: Opt-in idle pane suppression. The single finding claimed pre-ready Continue commands are lost. The agent argued they are no-ops against already-running panes, and added only a comment. The reasoning is plausible, but the packet does not show the code needed to rule out tmux-side pauses.
guidance_observations: The agent piled several law tokens onto a pushback whose real argument was about tmux's default pane state.

evidence: `for (let i = 0; i < 20 && t.sent.length < 2; i++) await Promise.resolve()` depends on the dispatch landing within 20 microtasks. The fix uses an auto-responding fake transport and awaits full resolution, which removes the magic count.
guidance_note: When a new await is inserted into a call path under test, change the fake to answer each command as it is sent instead of polling microtasks for the intermediate state.

narrative: Adds a version floor for requestReport. The one finding was a magic-count microtask poll in a test, introduced when the version probe added an await. The agent replaced it with an auto-responding fake, and the next round approved.

evidence: IMPL.md §2.1 said spawnTmux 'drives `tmux -CC`', but spawn.ts:29 returns `["-C", ...]` and spawn.ts:15-18 says -CC is refused. The agent admits 'My §2.1 line literally inverted the note it was placeholding'.
guidance_note: When writing a placeholder that summarizes a note being relocated, read the note's source anchor before paraphrasing it.

narrative: A planning doc for relocating library notes. The reviewer caught that the doc inverted the -C/-CC fact. The fix corrected it and aligned two other labels.

evidence: The nested ternary maps each mode string to the identical string, and this PR added a fourth branch. The fix adds an `isAppMode` type guard and reuses it in loadFromStorage, so membership is defined once.
guidance_note: When adding a variant to a chain that maps values to themselves, replace the chain with a membership guard instead of extending it.

narrative: The Console tab foundation. The one finding was an identity-mapping ternary that this PR extended. The agent replaced it with a type guard and also used that guard to deduplicate the persistence check.

evidence: The code has `.catch(() => {})` under a comment claiming it swallows 'only teardown-of-an-already-absent-resource', but an empty catch swallows everything. The fix logs each failure with context and rewrites the comment to match.
guidance_note: Don't write a comment claiming a catch is narrow unless the code narrows it; when writing an empty catch, log what it swallows from the start.

narrative: An escape-code playground. The reviewer correctly flagged empty teardown catches whose comment overclaimed their scope. The agent now logs the failures and corrected the comment.

evidence: The new store copied parsePaneList, captureSeeds, firstKey, now and both caps verbatim from scrollback-store.ts. Its own comment said the next consumer was the trigger to extract them, and this diff was that consumer. The fix extracts recording-capture.ts and imports it from both stores.
guidance_note: When your own comment names the condition for extracting shared code and your change meets that condition, do the extraction in the original PR.

narrative: The Moment Diff demo copied the capture infrastructure from another store, even though a comment in the code said to extract it at exactly this point. The agent extracted the identical pieces and deliberately kept the state machines that differ separate.
guidance_observations: The agent ignored an extraction trigger it had written itself.

evidence: linkedTimelines iterates `group.snapshots.keys()`, then `if (tl !== null)` guards a null that timelineFor can only return for a missing snapshot. The fix iterates entries and builds the timeline through one helper, which is the restructure option the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: When iterating a map's keys only to look each value up again, iterate the entries instead.

evidence: The reviewer says the if has no else and silently skips work. The agent shows both arms reach the same screen state (forward delta vs clear plus full paint), which the hunk's `if (prev !== null && cursorMs >= prev)` is consistent with. The usable part was moving strategy selection into a pure tested paintOp. The flag is a false positive: F1's fix 5aba3ee changed sync-engine.ts, not SyncSurface, and the packet shows no diff touching this effect.

narrative: The synchronized scrollback demo. Round 0 caught a defensive null guard over an impossible state, fixed by iterating entries. Round 1 misdescribed a forward-delta optimization as a silent skip. The agent corrected the premise and still turned the useful part into a pure paintOp, with tests. Round 1 was on pre-existing view code, not on the F1 fix.

evidence: `catch { return; }` on JSON.parse of a control frame left the viewer silently stuck. The server bridge's convention is to surface parse errors. The fix logs the error and moves status to 'error' with a message.
guidance_note: When writing a parse catch at a trust boundary, copy the sibling bridge's error-surfacing convention instead of returning silently.

narrative: The read-only pane mirror. A silent catch on control-frame parsing was flagged, and the agent made it surface in both the console and the UI status.

evidence: The in-loop `continue` for command-channel samples is a mild skip, not a bug. The filter/map rewrite is equivalent. Narrowing paneOutputCheck to PaneOutputMessage also removed a redundant inner isPaneOutput throw, a real tightening beyond the style point.

narrative: The protocol conformance dashboard. A style-level dataflow finding on a continue-skip was accepted. The fix also tightened a parameter type and removed a redundant guard.

evidence: The reviewer says the rejection reason is typed `unknown`. In TS lib types it is `any` (`onrejected?: (reason: any) => ...`), so the annotation narrows any rather than casting unknown. The reviewer's fix leaves `response: any`, with `.success` read unchecked, which is strictly weaker. The kernel, that the annotation is still an unchecked claim about the rejection shape, rests on the library's documented contract, which the packet does not show.

narrative: The collaborative pane demo had a single round. The reviewer misread TS's rejection typing and proposed dropping an annotation, which would have weakened types. The agent pushed back correctly with the lib signature and the sibling pattern.

evidence: `attempts` survives close()→connect(), which corrupts the next episode's budget. The reviewer's reset point, openSocket(), is also the reconnect timer's callback, so resetting there would make maxAttempts unreachable. 83afcb8 resets attempts and lastError in connect() and adds a regression test.
guidance_note: When moving lifecycle state onto a new state field, list every counter's reset point against each episode boundary (consumer connect vs timer retry) before submitting.

evidence: The test polled every 20ms for the drain notice, then asserted status 'ready', racing the server's 1s drain deadline. 83afcb8 captures the status and the rejection synchronously inside onDraining, which is the reviewer's first suggestion.
guidance_note: When asserting on a time-bounded window, sample inside the event callback that opens the window instead of polling and asserting later.

evidence: The idle→'connecting' imprecision predates this PR: the deleted mapToUnified already did `case "idle" → {status:"connecting"}`. Adding an idle variant is a cross-connector contract change, which the agent routed to ticket tmux-lifecycle-zng. The flag is a false positive: 83afcb8 only added resets in connect() and test changes, and did not touch the initial state.

This PR introduced the draining flag and cleared it only in openSocket(), so it stays true through the reconnect backoff and calls are rejected instead of queued. The agent cleared it in finalizeConnection alongside the other connection-scoped teardown. The flag is a false positive for a fix-caused finding: the bug is from the round-0 diff (`openSocket(){ this.draining = false; ...`), and 83afcb8 did not touch draining.
guidance_note: When introducing a connection-scoped flag, clear it at the same site that tears down the other connection-scoped fields (finalizeConnection), not at the next open.

narrative: Collapses the WebSocket client's dual state machine onto ConnectionState. Round 0 found a stale retry counter and a racy drain test. The agent correctly refused the reviewer's openSocket reset point, which would have made maxAttempts unreachable. Round 1 found a draining flag that survived into backoff, an original-PR bug, plus an idle-state imprecision from before this PR that was correctly deferred to a ticket. Neither round-1 finding came from the 83afcb8 fix.
guidance_observations: Round 1's draining bug was in the original diff and missed by round 0. Auditing every connection-scoped field's clearing site when the flag was introduced would have caught it before review.
